traits.name: Unbound
traits.effect: - Increase DMG by 350%; - Decrease SPA by 5%; - Increase Range by 10%; Single Placement
traits.restriction: Single placement: compare total team output before rerolling.
traits.why: The documented 350% damage amplification concentrates output into a single placement. Compare that one carry with the total output and coverage of the placements it replaces; it is not an automatic support or economy recommendation.

traits.name: Primordial
traits.effect: - Increase DMG by 35%; - Decrease SPA by 15%; - Increase Range by 20%
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: Damage, attack interval and range improve together without the documented single-placement restriction of Unbound. This gives damage units a broad alternative when multiple placements matter.

traits.name: Forsaken
traits.effect: - Increase Crit DMG by 35%; - Increase Crit Chance by 35%; - Increase Range by 10%
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: Critical chance and critical damage improve together. Value depends on the unit actually using critical attacks and its existing critical stats; a non-critical support kit does not gain the same benefit.

traits.name: Draconic
traits.effect: - Increase DMG by 20%; - Increase DoT Damage by 120%; - Decrease overall cost by 15%
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The large documented DoT bonus rewards a damaging status kit, while the cost reduction helps establish it earlier. A direct-hit unit without damaging DoT does not use the main reason for this grade.

traits.name: Investor
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The income increase addresses the economy slot rather than carry damage. Its value depends on bringing a money-farm unit and having enough remaining upgrades or waves to spend the extra income.

traits.name: Optics
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: Extra range can expand support coverage and keep more targets within a conditional aura. It does not supply direct damage or attack-speed bonuses, so evaluate actual map coverage before choosing it for a carry.

traits.name: Bolt
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The attack-interval reduction improves repeated attacks without requiring critical or DoT mechanics. It lacks Primordial’s accompanying damage and range bonuses, making it a narrower damage option.

traits.name: Precision 2
traits.effect: - Increase Critical Chance by 20%; - Increase Critical Damage by 10%
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: Its critical chance and critical damage bonuses favor kits that make meaningful use of critical attacks. It offers larger documented bonuses than Precision 1 but contributes little to non-attacking support effects.

traits.name: Precision 1
traits.effect: - Increase Critical Chance by 10%; - Increase Critical Damage by 5%
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The smaller critical package can serve a developing critical build. Its documented chance and damage bonuses are both below Precision 2; keep it for the relevant kit rather than treating it as a universal upgrade.

traits.name: Limit Breaker
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The documented 15% damage increase is a straightforward attacking-unit option. It lacks the attack interval, range or specialist DoT benefits that justify the higher role-fit grades.

traits.name: Range 2
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The 10% range increase can repair a particular placement or support-coverage gap. Optics supplies a larger range bonus, and extra reach has little value when the required targets are already covered.

traits.name: Speed 2
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The 10% attack-interval reduction supports repeated attacks. Bolt provides a larger documented reduction; this remains a useful interim choice when stronger rolls are unavailable.

traits.name: Strength 2
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: A 10% damage increase helps an attacking unit without demanding a specific mechanic. Limit Breaker provides a larger flat bonus, while specialist traits can address additional parts of a kit.

traits.name: Enlightenment
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: Extra experience helps account progression, but the documented effect does not directly improve damage, control or support during a stage. The low combat grade does not mean it has no leveling use.

traits.name: Range 1
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: A small range increase is useful only when it crosses a real coverage threshold. Larger range traits are preferable for a dedicated coverage build; do not reroll solely for a rarity label.

traits.name: Speed 1
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The 5% attack-interval reduction provides a modest interim attack-speed benefit. Speed 2 and Bolt offer larger documented reductions, so this is a low-investment stopping point rather than a finished build.

traits.name: Strength 1
traits.restriction: Role fit and actual unit mechanics determine value.
traits.why: The 5% damage increase is a modest interim damage roll. Stronger flat-damage traits and role-specific options provide more documented benefit; preserve resources if this unit will soon be replaced.
